correctness.rationale: On the whole ambient group, each Fourier character is one eigenvector of counting convolution. The ternary zero-sum filter gives the average of three products with local factors 2 at a frequency-symbol match and -1 otherwise, i.e. (-1)^n times the sum of three signed powers (-2)^(c_j) divided by 3. This is integer-valued because each power is 1 modulo 3; negation symmetry also gives real eigenvalues, whose moduli are the singular values. Divide a putative vanishing sum by the smallest signed power. A unique minimum leaves an odd integer; three minima leave 3; two minima force the remaining exponent to exceed the minimum by one. For n>=2 this gives exactly (m,m,m+1) up to permutation with m>=1 and n=3m+1. Counting ambient words gives the factor of three and the stated multinomial nullity. The normalized probability for one ordered count triple differs from the central equal-count probability at length 3m by (3m+1)/(3(m+1)); Stirling then gives the claimed constant and relative O(1/n) along the singular progression only. A separate phase-count check on dual coset representatives at n=2 through 7 gave nonzero ambient nullities only at 4 and 7, namely 36 and 630. value.rationale: The dipole is a canonical nowhere-zero flow family, and ambient counting convolution asks a natural recoverability question not answered by counting its flows. The exact singular progression, description of every invisible mode, and quantitative rate of loss give a usable rank classification across all lengths. The value is the cancellation and rank law, not the standard character filter; no claim is made about stable inversion away from zero or arbitrary graphs.
